title: Meridian Safety Systems — Final Round Bid Comparison
summary: Final round bid comparison for the exit of Meridian Safety Systems, prepared by ACP / Houlihan Lokey (strictly confidential). Three bids were received on March 30, 2018: Honeywell Safety at $268M EV (9.4x EBITDA, selected), 3M Safety Division at $252M EV (8.9x EBITDA, runner-up), and a PE sponsor at $244M EV (8.6x EBITDA, declined due to earnout and rollover requirements). Honeywell was recommended as the winning bidder based on highest value and greatest certainty of close, with a 100% cash, no-financing-condition stock purchase and anticipated close of April 15, 2018.

risks: financing risk on PE bid
earnout uncertainty on PE bid

title: Meridian Safety Systems — IOI Tracker
summary: First-round IOI tracker for Meridian Safety Systems, prepared by Houlihan Lokey, capturing seven bids received by March 2, 2018. Seven parties submitted indications — three shortlisted (Honeywell Safety Products at $260–280M / 9.2–9.9x selected as lead, 3M Safety Division at $240–265M / 8.5–9.3x, and Sponsor A at $230–255M / 8.1–9.0x). Four parties were not advanced due to low valuations, financing conditionality, strategic misfit, or financing concerns. Implied EV multiples ranged from 6.9x to 9.9x across all bidders, suggesting LTM EBITDA in the ~$28–29M range based on the leading bid.

title: Meridian Safety Systems — Management Presentation
summary: Management presentation prepared for final-round buyer meetings in March 2018 as part of the exit process for Meridian Safety Systems, Inc. The document covers Meridian's company overview, management team, strategy, value creation initiatives (roll-up M&A, SafeGuard private-label line, compliance services), and financial performance over the holding period (FY2012 entry through LTM Dec-2017). Meridian is a Columbus, OH-based regional distributor of industrial PPE and safety compliance solutions with $198M LTM revenue and $28.4M LTM Adj. EBITDA. Atlas Crossing Partners acquired the business in October 2012 and grew it through three bolt-on acquisitions plus organic growth.

growth_drivers: SafeGuard private-label expansion to 30%+ penetration (~$15M additional revenue)
Southeast and Texas DC expansion unlocking $30–40M incremental market
Compliance services scale-up adding 20 specialists for $15–18M incremental revenue
Digital ordering platform (launch 2019) with 18% higher revenue per customer peer benchmark
risks: Integration complexity from three bolt-on acquisitions
Founder/CEO dependency (Gary Thornton, 14 years, original founder)
Geographic concentration — Southeast/Texas markets underserved vs. local competitors

title: Meridian Safety Systems — Closing Checklist
summary: Closing checklist for the sale of Meridian Safety Systems by ACP Fund I to Honeywell, with a target close of April 15, 2018. All 20 items are marked Complete. Key closing events include: execution of the Stock Purchase Agreement (Apr 9), HSR early termination granted by DOJ (Apr 25), debt payoff of $82M to First Eagle Alt. Capital, purchase price wire of $268M from Honeywell, R&W insurance policy bound at $13.4M limit, $89M net proceeds wired to ACP Fund I, $13.4M indemnity holdback escrowed at JPMorgan (18-month term), and $102M total LP distribution issued April 20, 2018. title: Meridian Safety Systems — Funds Flow Memorandum
summary: Closing funds flow memorandum prepared by Latham & Watkins LLP for the sale of Meridian Safety Systems to Honeywell on April 15, 2018. Enterprise value of $268M; net debt of $82.1M repaid to First Eagle; transaction expenses of ~$8M (Houlihan Lokey, Latham & Watkins, RSM US); $13.4M indemnity holdback in escrow (18-month tail). Net equity proceeds of $164.3M flow to ACP Fund I. ACP waterfall: $32M return of capital, $18.9M preferred return at 8%, then 80/20 LP/GP carry split on remaining $113.4M, yielding $141.6M cumulative LP distributions and $22.7M GP carry.

title: Meridian Safety Systems — HSR Filing Summary
summary: HSR Filing Summary prepared by Latham & Watkins LLP in April 2018 for the acquisition of Meridian Safety Systems by Honeywell Safety Products (Honeywell International Inc.) at a transaction value of $268M. The filing was deemed HSR-reportable, with both parties filing simultaneously on April 10, 2018. Early termination was granted by the DOJ Antitrust Division on April 15 (Day 15 of the 30-day waiting period), clearing the transaction to close. The competition analysis found minimal antitrust risk due to a vertical (manufacturer-to-distributor) rather than horizontal relationship between Honeywell and Meridian, with no meaningful HHI concentration concerns. The transaction closed April 15, 2018.

key_quotes.quote: Honeywell manufactures safety equipment; Meridian distributes — minimal horizontal overlap
The transaction presents minimal antitrust risk... The vertical integration presents limited horizontal overlap and no market concentration concerns under HHI analysis.

title: Meridian Safety Systems — Sell-Side Quality of Earnings Summary
summary: RSM US LLP prepared a vendor due diligence quality of earnings (QofE) analysis for Meridian Safety Systems on behalf of Atlas Crossing Partners (ACP) and Houlihan Lokey in support of a sale process. The report covers LTM December 2017 and presents an adjusted EBITDA bridge from reported EBITDA of $23.8M to a preliminary adjusted EBITDA of $28.4M (total addbacks of $4.6M). Key findings affirm high revenue quality (91% from accounts with >2-year tenure, no single customer >5% of revenue), supportable and well-documented addbacks, stable working capital (NWC peg of $27.2M at ~14% of revenue), and a validated structural gross margin premium for the proprietary SafeGuard product line (41.3% vs. 35.8% for branded).

key_quotes.quote: 91% of LTM revenue from accounts with >2-year tenure. Top 50 customers represent 52% of revenue; all 50 have been customers for >3 years. No single customer exceeds 5% of revenue.
Total addbacks of $4.6M against reported EBITDA of $23.8M are evidenced by third-party invoices and internal tracking.
SafeGuard gross margin of 41.3% vs. 35.8% for branded — a 550bps premium. Margin advantage driven by proprietary specification lock-in and preferred manufacturing agreements.
NWC as % of revenue has been stable at 13.8–14.5% over FY15–LTM. Proposed NWC peg of $27.2M reflects trailing-12-month average.

growth_drivers: Compliance-driven recurring customer base (91% of revenue from accounts with >2-year tenure)
Proprietary SafeGuard product line with 550bps gross margin premium vs. branded
Preferred manufacturing agreements underpinning structural margin advantage
risks: CEO compensation was above-market (Thornton family; addback required)
Recent Gulf Coast Safety Group acquisition integration costs
Q4 2017 revenue timing benefit from customer prepayment (pull-forward; reversed in bridge)

title: Meridian Safety Systems — VDD Financial Analysis (RSM US)
summary: Sell-side vendor due diligence financial model prepared by RSM US for Meridian Safety Systems, covering LTM December 2017 and historical financials from FY12–FY16. Revenue grew from $72M in FY12 to $198M LTM Dec-17, implying strong historical growth. LTM Adj. EBITDA is calculated but left blank in the rendered workbook; estimated from components at approximately $24.4M after adjustments.

growth_drivers: Strong organic revenue growth from $72M (FY12) to $198M (LTM Dec-17)
Consistent top-line expansion across all periods
risks: Multiple normalizing adjustments to EBITDA suggest recurring non-recurring items
CEO compensation excess adjustment indicates potential governance/comp structure concerns
Revenue timing adjustment in LTM period

title: Project Summit — Confidential Information Memorandum: Meridian Safety Systems, Inc.
summary: Sell-side CIM prepared by Houlihan Lokey on behalf of Atlas Crossing Partners Fund I for the exit of Meridian Safety Systems, Inc. ("Project Summit"). Meridian is a Midwest/Appalachia/Gulf Coast regional distributor of industrial PPE, fall protection, gas detection equipment, and safety compliance solutions, serving 6,400+ customers across oil & gas, construction, utilities, and chemical manufacturing. ACP acquired the business in 2012 at ~$72M revenue and grew it to $198M LTM revenue and $28.4M Adj. EBITDA through three bolt-on acquisitions, private-label (SafeGuard) expansion, and a compliance-services build-out. The process is a 100% sale with IOI deadline March 2, 2018 and anticipated close April 15, 2018.

key_quotes.quote: Compliance schedules — not capex cycles — drive replacement demand, creating a durable, predictable revenue stream largely immune to macro conditions. Customer renewal rate of 91% in LTM 2017.
SafeGuard grew from 6% of revenue at entry to 22% in LTM 2017, carrying a 550bps gross margin premium vs. comparable branded product.
3 bolt-ons acquired at average 5.2x pre-synergy EBITDA; integrated within 15 months each.
Meridian's safety training and compliance audit practice grew from zero at entry to $8.4M in LTM revenue (4.2% of total) at 24% gross margins — significantly above distribution margins.

growth_drivers: Roll-up M&A playbook with three bolt-ons acquired at average 5.2x pre-synergy EBITDA
SafeGuard private-label expansion (6% → 22% of revenue; 550bps GM premium vs. branded)
Compliance-services revenue build-out ($8.4M LTM, 4.2% of total, 24% gross margin)
Non-discretionary OSHA/MSHA/EPA compliance-driven replacement demand
Regional distribution density (8 DCs, next-day delivery to >85% of customer base)
High customer renewal rate (91% LTM 2017) and average tenure of 9.2 years
risks: Customer concentration risk in oil & gas and construction end markets (cyclical exposure)
Integration risk from ongoing bolt-on strategy for successor owner
Private-label competition pressure from branded distributors
Regulatory exposure — business model dependent on OSHA/MSHA/EPA mandates remaining in force

title: Meridian Safety Systems — Final Returns Summary
summary: Final returns summary for Meridian Safety Systems, an industrial PPE & safety compliance distributor held by Atlas Crossing Partners Fund I from October 2012 to April 2018 (5.5-year hold). The company was exited via strategic sale to Honeywell Safety Products for an exit EV of $268M (9.4x EBITDA), versus an entry EV of $95M (6.6x). EBITDA from $9M to $28.4M.

title: Investment Committee Memorandum — Initial Investment Recommendation: Meridian Safety Systems, Inc.
summary: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund I entry IC memo recommending acquisition of Meridian Safety Systems, Inc., a Columbus, OH-based industrial PPE and safety compliance distributor, at a $95M enterprise value (6.6x LTM Adj. EBITDA of $9.0M). The memo outlines a roll-up thesis targeting 10 bolt-on acquisitions in the Permian Basin, Gulf Coast, and Southeast, private-label expansion via the SafeGuard brand, and a compliance services build-out. Base case underwrites 2.8x MOIC / 20% IRR at a $268M exit EV over a 5–6-year hold. Atlas Crossing equity commitment is $32M against $63M in senior debt from Madison Capital.

key_quotes.quote: We see a clear path to 2.5–3.5x MOIC over a 5–6-year hold through geographic roll-up M&A, private-label (SafeGuard) launch and scaling, and a compliance-services build-out that leverages Meridian's OSHA-certified specialist team.

The US industrial PPE distribution market is highly fragmented — estimated 800+ distributors with <$30M revenue each. Meridian has $72M in revenue and 3 DCs, making it the dominant player in its current Ohio-Appalachian-Gulf geography.
Launching a SafeGuard private-label line targeting 20–25% penetration by Year 4 implies 200–300bps gross margin expansion vs. current 32.1% LTM gross margin.

OSHA, MSHA, and EPA regulations mandate ongoing PPE and safety system purchases. Meridian's customers cannot defer inspection or replacement cycles — non-compliance results in facility shutdowns and legal liability. 87% of FY12 revenue is from repeat accounts; average customer tenure is 7.2 years.

CEO Gary Thornton founded Meridian in 1998 and has grown it from $8M to $72M organically. Thornton is rolling 25% of his proceeds. We are co-investing in a new CFO (Priya Nair, ex-Deloitte) and Head of M&A Integration in Year 1.

growth_drivers: Geographic roll-up M&A targeting 10 bolt-on acquisitions in Permian Basin, Gulf Coast, and Southeast
SafeGuard private-label line targeting 20–25% penetration by Year 4 with 200–300bps gross margin expansion
Compliance audit and safety training service offering targeting $3–5M annual revenue at 22–25% gross margin by Year 3
Non-discretionary, regulatory-mandated demand (OSHA/MSHA/EPA) driving repeat revenue (87% from accounts >2 yrs tenure)
New CFO hire and VP M&A Integration to support operational scaling
risks: Energy market cyclicality: 32% of revenue from oil & gas
Integration execution risk across 3+ bolt-ons in 5 years
Private-label brand acceptance risk for SafeGuard in established branded PPE category
OSHA-certified technician labor market tightness
